{{Short description|Compactness theorem in Yang–Mills theory}}
In [[differential geometry]] and in particular [[Yang–Mills theory]], '''Uhlenbeck's compactness theorem''' is a result about [[Sequence|sequences]] of (weak Yang–Mills) connections with uniformly bounded [[Curvature form|curvature]] having weakly or [[Uniform convergence|uniformly convergent]] subsequences up to [[Gauge theory|gauge]]. It is an important theorem used in the [[Compactification (mathematics)|compactification]] of the anti self-dual Yang–Mills moduli space (ASDYM moduli space), which is central to the construction of [[Donaldson invariant|Donaldson invariants]] on four-dimensional [[Smooth manifold|manifolds]] (short [[4-manifold]]) or [[monopole Floer homology]] on three-dimensional manifolds (short [[3-manifold]]). The theorem is named after [[Karen Uhlenbeck]], who first described it in 1982. In 2019, Uhlenbeck became the first woman to be awarded the [[Abel Prize]], in part for her contributions to [[Partial differential equation|partial differential equations]] and [[gauge theory]].<ref name="citation">{{cite web |title=2019: Karen Keskulla Uhlenbeck |url=https://abelprize.no/abel-prize-laureates/2019 |access-date=22 July 2022 |publisher=The Abel Prize}}</ref> Uhlenbeck's compactness theorem was generalized to [[Yang–Mills flow|Yang–Mills flows]] by Alex Waldron in 2018.

== Uhlenbeck's weak compactness theorem ==
Let <math>X</math> be a <math>n</math>-[[Dimension|dimensional]] [[Compact space|compact]] [[Riemannian manifold]] and <math>P\twoheadrightarrow X</math> be a [[Principal bundle|principal <math>G</math>-bundle]] with a compact [[Lie group]] <math>G</math>. Let <math>1<p<\infty</math> with <math>p>n/2</math> and let <math>(A_m)_{m\in\mathbb{N}}\in\mathcal{A}^{1,p}(P)
:=W^{1,p}(X,\operatorname{Ad}(P))\subset L^p(X,\operatorname{Ad}(P))</math> be a [[sequence]] of [[Sobolev space|Sobolev]] [[Connection (principal bundle)|connections]] with uniform bound for <math>\|F_{A_m}\|_p</math>, the [[Norm (mathematics)|norm]] of their [[Curvature form|curvatures]]. Then there exists a sequence <math>u_m\in\mathcal{G}^{2,p}(P)</math> of [[gauge transformations]], so that <math>u_m^*A_m</math> [[Weak convergence (Hilbert space)|converges weakly]]. In other words, any <math>L^p</math>-[[Bounded set|bounded]] subset of <math>\mathcal{A}^{1,p}(P)/\mathcal{G}^{2,p}(P)</math> is [[weak topology|weakly compact]].<ref>Uhlenbeck 1982, Theorem 1.5 (3.6).</ref><ref>Wehrheim 2004, Theorem A</ref>

== Uhlenbeck's strong compactness theorem ==
Let <math>X</math> be a <math>n</math>-[[Dimension|dimensional]] [[Compact space|compact]] [[Riemannian manifold]] and <math>P\twoheadrightarrow X</math> be a [[Principal bundle|principal <math>G</math>-bundle]] with a compact [[Lie group]] <math>G</math>. Let <math>1<p<\infty</math> with <math>p>n/2</math> and <math>p>4/3</math> if <math>n=2</math>. Let <math>(A_m)_{m\in\mathbb{N}}\in\mathcal{A}^{1,p}(P)
:=W^{1,p}(X,\operatorname{Ad}(P))\subset L^p(X,\operatorname{Ad}(P))</math> be a sequence of [[Weak solution|weak]] [[Yang–Mills connections]], hence so that:

: <math>\int_X\langle F_{A_m},\mathrm{d}_{A_m}\beta\rangle\mathrm{d}\operatorname{vol}_g=0</math>

for all <math>m\in\mathbb{N}</math> and <math>\beta\in\mathcal{A}^{1,p}(P)</math>, with uniform bound for <math>\|F_{A_m}\|_p</math>. Then there exists a [[subsequence]], also denoted <math>(A_m)_{m\in\mathbb{N}}</math>, and a sequence <math>u_m\in\mathcal{G}^{2,p}(P)</math> of gauge transformations, so that <math>u_m^*A_m</math> [[Uniform convergence|converges uniformly]] to a smooth connection <math>A\in\mathcal{A}(P)</math>.<ref>Wehrheim 2004, Theorem E</ref> (Uhlenbeck's strong compactness theorem is not stated explicitly in Uhlenbeck's 1982 paper, but follows from the results within.)
